[Verse 1]
She’s wild as the open plain,
Untamed and running true…
Her hooves are thunder on the earth,
The sky bends close to view.
She kicks against the fences,
She won’t be tied or tamed,
A streak of fire and starlight dust,
Too bright to hold or name.
He moves like patient mountains,
A moose in quiet grace,
With ancient power in his bones
And stillness on his face.
He does not need loud shouting,
His strength is in his frame,
A steady shadow at her side,
A calm and rooted flame.
She’s wildfire on the valley wind,
He’s forests standing wide,
Together all the world can feel
The pull of their twin tides.
[Pre-Chorus]
Not superficial, a deeper role…
They’re born to walk as one,
Two halves of one bright soul.
The way she runs,
The way he knows…
A wild stampede, a silent guard,
Together, how they grow.
[Chorus]
They turn their contrasts into strength,
They heal from every scar…
They’re blazing constellations of who they are.
The mustang heart, the antlered crown,
A fire and northern star…
They are the storm that steers the heart.
[Verse 2]
She feels the winds before they rise,
She knows the hidden trails,
She dances on the razor edge
Where every courage sails.
Her laughter cracks the granite sky,
Her mane in restless flight,
She is the mustang kicking dust,
A comet in the night.
From him she learns a steady pace,
To breathe on solid ground,
To hear the softer songs of strength
Inside a smaller sound.
He walks like rivers under ice,
So quiet, deep, and wide,
A moose with antlers crowned in dusk,
Old forests at his side.
His silent watch, his anchored stance
Turn down her doubt to peace,
His gentle gaze, his rooted spine
Let all her tremors cease.
She teaches him the leap of faith,
To trust the wild unseen,
Her fearless charge through storm and flame
Keeps every heartbeat keen.
[Pre-Chorus]
Not superficial, a deeper role…
Their different ways still make them whole.
A mustang flame,
A river’s flow…
They bend the world with how they love,
They rise and make it glow.
[Chorus]
Every struggle, every scar
Built constellations of who they are.
Her wildfire spirit burning fast,
His silent force that always lasts.
The mustang heart, the moose’s crest,
They are the storm that holds its breath.
[Verse 3]
When her bright fire starts to fade,
He’s forest, wide and tall,
His quiet shadows wrap her flame
And gently break her fall.
When questions crowd her restless mind
And every path seems wrong,
He stands there like a northern pine,
Her shelter standing strong.
When his broad shoulders feel too worn
And all his strength feels thin,
Her wild-eyed grin cuts through the dark
And shakes the night within.
She circles back on pounding hooves,
A streak of dust and light,
Her faith crashes against his doubt
And sets his spirit right.
When she feels small, a trembling flame,
His gaze reveals her star,
He sees the wild she can’t recall,
The truth of who she are.
When he feels lost, a quiet ghost,
She will not let him fade,
Her reckless trust wraps round his ribs
And says he’s surely made.
[Bridge]
Not superficial, a deeper role…
Their woven lives have shaped a whole.
A mustang running toward the sky,
A moose with steady stride.
Their love keeps roaring through the years,
A tide that will not hide.
Through all the days that lie ahead
Their tracks will twist and blend:
Her thunder hooves, his rooted stance,
Two paths that never end.
Her fire still burns when nights grow cold,
His calm outlasts the storm,
They lift each other when they fall,
They keep one lantern warm.
They won’t be perfect, learning too,
Still stumbling as they go,
But stubbornly, through every storm,
They’ll stay and let love grow.
[Pre-Chorus]
Not superficial, a deeper role…
Their woven lives have shaped a whole.
The mustang flame,
The river’s flow…
They give each other strength to rise,
They’re how true lovers grow.
[Chorus]
Every struggle, every scar
Writes constellations of who they are.
Wildfire spirit, antlered crest,
They’re more than most, they are the best.
The mustang heart, the moose’s rest,
Two reckless souls that pass the test.
They are the blaze, they are the art,
The mustang and the moose’s heart.
